comparisons.scheme1_value: Farmers (owner cultivators, tenant farmers, sharecroppers, SHGs/JLGs) for crop cultivation, post-harvest expenses, farm equipment, and allied agricultural activities.
comparisons.scheme2_value: Non-farm micro entrepreneurs (shopkeepers, vendors, artisans, food services, repair shops, etc.) and allied-agriculture activities (poultry, dairy, beekeeping) for income-generating businesses.

comparisons.scheme1_value: Starts with: Scale of finance for crop × area cultivated + 10% for post-harvest + 20% for repairs/maintenance + insurance. Increases 10% annually for 5 years. No upper cap mentioned; depends on farm size.
comparisons.scheme2_value: Tiered: Shishu (up to ₹50k) → Kishore (₹50k–₹5 lakh) → Tarun (₹5–₹10 lakh) → Tarun Plus (up to ₹20 lakh for successful repeat borrowers).

comparisons.scheme1_value: Effective rate ~4% per annum (2% government interest subvention + 3% prompt repayment incentive). **Catch:** Lose 3% incentive if repayment is delayed; actual rate becomes costlier.
comparisons.scheme2_value: Rates set by individual lenders per RBI guidelines—varies by bank/MFI. Upfront fees/processing charges waived for Shishu loans by most banks.

comparisons.scheme1_value: Farmers (individual/joint borrowers), tenant farmers, sharecroppers, SHGs/JLGs of farmers. Must be engaged in agriculture.
comparisons.scheme2_value: Individuals, proprietorships, partnerships, companies. Must not be a defaulter to any bank/FI and have satisfactory credit history. Skills/experience assessed per activity type.

comparisons.scheme1_value: Application form, 2 passport photos, ID proof (Driving Licence/Aadhaar/Voter ID/Passport), address proof, proof of landholding certified by revenue authorities, cropping pattern with acreage.
comparisons.scheme2_value: **Shishu:** Identity proof (self-attested), residence proof (recent utility bill/property tax/Aadhaar), 2 colour photos, quotation of items to buy, business proof if any.

comparisons.scheme1_value: For limits >₹1.60 lakh/₹3.00 lakh: collateral security documents required (bank-specific).
comparisons.scheme2_value: **Kishore/Tarun/Tarun Plus:** Last 6 months' bank statements, last 2 years' balance sheets + IT/sales tax returns (₹2 lakh+), projected balance sheet, sales figures, project report, partnership/company documents, asset-liability statements.

comparisons.scheme1_value: Visit bank website or Jan Samarth portal → Select KCC → Fill form → Get reference number → Bank contacts within 3–4 working days → Final sanction at branch.
comparisons.scheme2_value: Go to udyamimitra.in or mudra.org.in → Click 'Apply Now' → Register (name, email, mobile + OTP) → Fill personal & business details → Choose loan tier → Attach documents → Submit. Also available via Jan Samarth & bank branches.

comparisons.scheme1_value: No fixed deadline. Apply anytime through your bank.
comparisons.scheme2_value: No deadline. Apply anytime online or at bank branches.

comparisons.scheme1_value: RuPay/ATM-enabled card usable at ATMs, micro-ATMs, PoS at input dealers, and mobile banking for accessing credit.
comparisons.scheme2_value: No card mentioned; loans disbursed to bank account per lender process.

comparisons.scheme1_value: **Interest subvention depends on prompt repayment.** Late payment = lose 3% incentive = loan becomes much costlier.
comparisons.scheme2_value: **No agents or middlemen allowed.** Anyone claiming to be a MUDRA agent is a fraud; apply only via official portals or bank branches.

comparisons.scheme1_value: **Collateral required for larger loans** (>₹1.60 lakh/₹3.00 lakh as per bank rules).
comparisons.scheme2_value: **Defaulters are not eligible.** If you defaulted on any bank/financial institution loan, you cannot apply.

comparisons.scheme1_value: **Bank discretion:** Exact terms vary by bank and location; not all banks may offer identical conditions.
comparisons.scheme2_value: **Interest rates vary.** Shop around and compare rates across lenders before applying.
Udyamimitra: udyamimitra.in | MUDRA: mudra.org.in | Jan Samarth: jansamarth.in

recommendation: **Choose KCC if:** You are a farmer (any size, tenant, sharecropper, or farm group) needing credit for crops, farm equipment, or farm-linked activities. Interest is heavily subsidised (~4%) if you repay on time. **Choose PMMY if:** You run a non-farm micro business (shop, service, craft, etc.) or allied-agriculture activity (dairy, poultry, beekeeping) that needs working capital or equipment. You have no fixed collateral but want small to medium loans (₹50k–₹20 lakh). **Key Difference:** KCC is **farm-focused with low, fixed interest**; PMMY is **business-focused with variable rates but easier collateral rules for small loans**. **Important:** This is AI guidance only. For final decisions, check official websites (mudra.org.in, myscheme.gov.in, jansamarth.in) and visit your bank or local loan center. Do not trust any unofficial agents.
